title: Token Gateway
summary: A narrowly scoped gateway that verifies signed workload tokens, enforces audience policy, and emits privacy-bounded audit decisions.
intended_users: Platform teams connecting short-lived internal workloads across trust zones.

design_decisions.problem_or_constraint: Internal services duplicated token verification and disagreed on audience, clock skew, and replay behavior.
design_decisions.alternatives_considered: Library-only verification was rejected because rollout drift remained. A service mesh plugin was deferred because the pilot environment lacks consistent mesh coverage.
design_decisions.chosen_approach_and_rationale: Centralize a small verification gateway with typed failure codes and fail-closed defaults.
design_decisions.accepted_trade_off: The gateway adds a network hop and its replay cache must remain available or reject traffic.
design_decisions.validation_approach: Table-driven tests cover expired tokens, wrong audience, algorithm confusion, unknown keys, clock boundaries, replay, malformed input, and audit redaction.
design_decisions.reconsideration_conditions: Move verification into a mesh policy only after equivalent conformance tests pass across every workload environment.

testing_strategy: Go table tests specify adversarial claim, cryptographic configuration, replay, parsing, and audit cases. Finch does not execute them.
security_threat: An attacker replays a stolen token or exploits algorithm/key confusion to impersonate a workload. Pinned algorithms, issuer/audience allowlists, bounded parsing, short lifetimes, nonce replay protection, and redacted auditing fail closed. Residual risk: A replay-cache outage causes denial of service; key-compromise response requires operator rotation.
production_limitation: The in-memory replay cache is single-region and intentionally fails closed during cache uncertainty.
technical_debt: Implement replicated nonce storage and automate issuer-key rotation drills.
track_alignment_explanation: The project exists to prevent a concrete workload-identity threat and documents attacker goals, false-rejection risk, containment, and operational harm.

ai_disclosure.purposes: Codex was used to author this deliberately synthetic calibration fixture and its structured submission answers.
ai_disclosure.substantially_generated_areas: All fixture source, documentation, tests, and submission narratives are synthetic and AI-assisted.
ai_disclosure.review_validation: The calibration operator reviews files for intended evidence strength, consistency, and absence of real secrets before pinning the commit.
ai_disclosure.rejected_or_changed_suggestion: Generic claims of runtime correctness were rejected because Finch performs static evidence review only.

ai_disclosure_narrative: This entire project is synthetic AI-assisted test data. It represents no participant, deployed product, or real credential.
